dispute.raised_at: generators/DISAGREEMENTS.md in this repository, 2026-10-01, and the KERI review panel of the CESR catalogue (finding SEC-F4); not yet raised with the CESR specification working group.
dispute.summary: The Annex indexed code table gives 2B#### (Ed25519 indexed sig big current only) an ondex field of two characters and states no constraint on its value, so a stream carrying ondex 9 decodes to index 70, ondex 9. keripy main (9a8b7aa7) rejects it: Indexer raises 'Invalid ondex=9 for code=2B' because keripy requires the ondex of every current-only code to be zero (src/keri/core/indexing.py, the IdxCrtSigDex checks in _exfil and _bexfil). The question has a KERI-layer dimension (review finding SEC-F4): neither the CESR nor the KERI specification says what an ondex on a current-only signature means, and keripy's own semantics exist only in its CESR layer, while its KERI-layer exposeds() indexes the prior next-key digests with whatever ondex a signature carries. An implementation that decodes the field as the table allows and reuses that KERI logic could count a current-only signature toward the prior-next threshold where keripy rejects the stream, so validators could disagree about one controller-signed event. The review's verifier judged this a controller-induced interop divergence rather than a way for an unauthorized key to gain weight. The specification should state whether a current-only code's ondex must be zero (making this a must-reject stream under a new case id) or what it means.

title: Parse a big current-only Ed25519 signature whose ondex field is not zero
